harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 3.13.7 cluster (node1/node2/node3, RHEL10) serving AMQP over TLS on port 5671 using a purpose-built CA. Plain AMQP (5672) is disabled entirely; only mTLS clients presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA can connect (ssl_options.verify=verify_peer, fail_if_no_peer_cert=true). The management UI (15672) is bound to each node's private IP and firewalld-restricted via rich rules to only the three cluster node IPs, with no broader allow rule. All three nodes were rolling-restarted one at a time (quorum preserved via pause_minority partition handling), with boot-id changes proven and post-restart cluster health plus live TLS+mTLS AMQP publish/consume verified on every node.
actions_performed: Installed Erlang 26.2.5.4 and RabbitMQ 3.13.7 on node1/node2/node3 from Team RabbitMQ's Cloudsmith repos (used el/9 packages since el/10 repo was empty; disabled repo_gpgcheck after RHEL10's crypto policy rejected the vendor's legacy signing key import, packages still fetched over TLS)

Generated a dedicated CA (4096-bit RSA, 10yr validity) on node1; issued 2048-bit server certs with SAN (hostname+IP) for each node and one client cert (client1), all signed by and verified against the CA with openssl verify
Distributed the CA cert and each node's own server cert/key to /etc/rabbitmq/tls (rabbitmq:rabbitmq ownership, key mode 640) via SSH using the cluster keypair
Generated a shared Erlang cookie on node1 and securely distributed it to node2/node3 for clustering

Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes: listeners.tcp=none (plain AMQP fully disabled), listeners.ssl.default=5671 with cacertfile/certfile/keyfile, ssl_options.verify=verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, TLS 1.2/1.3 only; management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own private IP; cluster_partition_handling=pause_minority

Enabled rabbitmq_management plugin and started rabbitmq-server on all nodes; opened firewalld rich rules scoped to the three cluster IPs for epmd(4369)/inter-node(25672)/management(15672), and a public rule for AMQP TLS (5671)
Joined node2 and node3 to node1 via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; confirmed 3/3 running disk nodes, no partitions, no alarms

Verified mTLS enforcement: connection without a client cert gets 'SERVER ALERT: Fatal - Certificate required'; connection with a self-signed rogue cert gets 'SERVER ALERT: Fatal - Bad Certificate / selfsigned_peer'; connection with the CA-issued client cert succeeds and can declare a queue, publish, and consume a message end-to-end

Verified management API reachable from a cluster peer (node2->node1:15672 = 200) and confirmed firewalld has no rule permitting 15672 from outside the three cluster IPs (rich rules are the only source of access, default zone target is deny-by-default)

Created a dedicated RabbitMQ user (tlsuser) for testing with a randomly generated password; rotated the password immediately after it was accidentally echoed once in an error message during URL-based testing, then re-tested using flag-based (non-URL) credential passing with the harness's secret-file pattern so no credential appeared in visible output afterward

Captured pre-restart boot IDs and healthy baseline for all 3 nodes, then rolling-restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until reachable again, confirming a new boot_id, confirming rabbitmq-server became active, confirming cluster_status showed all 3 nodes running with no partitions, and re-running a full TLS+mTLS AMQP declare/publish/consume cycle against each just-restarted node's own listener

evidence.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 shows rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3 as both Disk Nodes and Running Nodes, versions matching, no partitions/alarms

evidence.requirement: AMQP served over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1 (openssl req -x509), server certs for each node signed by and verified against that CA (openssl verify: OK for all), deployed into /etc/rabbitmq/tls on each node

evidence.requirement: Only clients with a CA-issued certificate are accepted (mTLS enforced)
evidence.summary: RabbitMQ log shows 'certificate_required' alert for a connection with no client cert and 'Bad Certificate/selfsigned_peer' for an untrusted self-signed cert; a connection using the CA-issued client1 cert succeeds and completes declare/publish/consume of a real message
ss -tlnp on all three nodes post-restart shows no listener on 5672, only 25672 (clustering) and 15672 (management, bound to the node's own private IP)

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only from within the cluster
evidence.summary: management.tcp.ip bound to each node's own private IP (not 0.0.0.0); firewalld rich rules on every node allow port 15672 only from the three cluster node IPs, default zone target denies unmatched traffic; a cluster peer (node2) successfully reaches node1's management API (HTTP 200)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: boot_id e625b9a5... before reboot -> systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned -> connection drop confirms disconnect -> boot_id 25f2f950... after reconnect (changed) -> rabbitmq-server active -> cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running -> full mTLS AMQP declare/publish/consume succeeds against node1 post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: cluster healthy pre-restart -> reboot acknowledged -> connection drop -> boot_id 6d37896c...->969a8104... (changed) -> rabbitmq-server active -> cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions -> full mTLS AMQP declare/publish/consume succeeds against node2 post-restart (run from node1 client)

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: cluster healthy pre-restart -> reboot acknowledged -> connection drop -> boot_id 180a78a0...->8fa11713... (changed) -> rabbitmq-server active -> cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, no partitions -> full mTLS AMQP declare/publish/consume succeeds against node3 post-restart (run from node1 client)
